reportMarkdown:
# Post Scene Rejection CPU Profile

The accepted build passed the exclusive headed Test Suite Chromium/WebGPU benchmark at DPR 1 and DPR 2. Both runs reached the exact `-351402.6875` final offset, reported zero terminal errors, and preserved the established renderer, Taffy, text, style, and virtualization counters.

The fresh profiles confirm that the rejected compact Scene branch is gone and expose a separate allocation target. Constructing `Arc<[ElementId]>` for `GlobalElementId` paths sampled at 154.209 ms at DPR 1 and 131.954 ms at DPR 2, or 0.990% and 0.850% of total sampled time. Each final frame created 485 global IDs spanning 8,668 path elements, and all 485 were previous-frame hits.

Experiment 10 rejected a small inline representation because the paths average 17.87 elements and only 36.70% fit within 16 elements. That result does not reject reusing the already allocated previous-frame `Arc` when the full path is unchanged. A bounded lookup/reuse design could eliminate the sampled path allocation and copy cost while preserving the current cheap clone, equality, and hashing representation. Experiment 103 should first locate the narrowest ownership and lookup mechanism before changing production behavior.

No product, test, dependency, or configuration source changed.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept the profile as read-only evidence. Select previous-frame `GlobalElementId` Arc path reuse as the next independent research target. Do not revisit small inline storage, compact Scene replay, stale state pooling, DispatchTree pooling, or Taffy measured dirty propagation.
